No roll ran on a v5 kernel, and a real machine restart was not timed.

No experiment built the report, or the gate that keeps clients and the next roll step away until the gap closes.

OBJ.why: There is no election: the first server back takes the lease by a conditional PUT (1.37 ms p50 on MinIO; about 30 ms on S3, cited) and loads the manifest. A restart-all was not run, and how long it waits for the old lease is not stated.

default.why: On this box three cold TS Raft processes with 20 groups are writable in 265 to 318 ms when the first one campaigns at once, and 20 dormant groups in a live process in 10 to 16 ms (E-26). The real machine start was not timed: v4's whole wake took 1.4 s against the 1.5 s bar, so the bar is tight wherever the project's own server must start, which is every row but the pooled one.

default.why: A resource is made by one committed catalog entry, and its seed is written once through the group's log, with 'seed applied' kept in the catalog row (DESIGN-V5 §4.2). A joining copy folds the log or a snapshot and never writes a seed of its own, and one log per group means a removed row cannot come back from another copy. E-33 shows a project founds one cluster with A-08.

V4.why: v4 fails the regression today: a fresh member's seed brings back a row the cluster deleted, in 2 runs of 2 (STATUS.md), because LWW with collected tombstones cannot tell 'never had' from 'deleted'. J's fix, a joining copy skips its seed, fits v4's join by ballot and is not built.
V4.closes: the skip-seed-on-join fix in v4, with the regression test

BUY.why: On JetStream the seed is a publish by whichever process creates the stream, so two creators both seed unless the publish carries an expected-sequence check. E-44 ran no seed.
BUY.closes: a seed test on the JetStream prototype

default.why: Members are named by id in each group's configuration, and the member record holds a listen and an advertised address, so a changed address keeps membership by design (DESIGN-V5 §6.1, need 7). No experiment tested addresses, IPv6 or a moved machine, and no axis of the map separates the rows here.
default.closes: address tests in phase 2 (L0 transport and member records)

V4.why: v4 parses bracketed IPv6 everywhere since V4-61, but it has no bind address apart from the advertised name, and on Fly the private IPv6 changes when a machine moves (STATUS.md).
V4.closes: a listen and advertise split in v4, with the address tests

default.why: Any server takes a client's write and forwards it to the group's leader (Y `fwd`; the `smart` rows keep `fwd` for browsers), and reads come from any ready replica or are passed on, so one public address in front of the copies reaches every resource. E-40 measured a client on one wss address reaching its first committed write in 13 to 17 ms. A TS edge takes a TLS terminator in front (A-11; E-27: 538 MB for 10,000 TLS links without one).

V4.why: v4 forwards from any member, but the link is cleartext after the handshake and a client redials members at their own addresses; STATUS.md lists TLS for clients and a one-address client mode as needs.

BUY.closes: E-44's checks run again through one TLS address

V4.why: v4 refuses a contract change by design: a peer whose methods, validation text or ring differs is refused, so such a deploy stops and starts every member (STATUS.md; DESIGN-DOOR §4).

default.why: The gate is a field the writer checks before it takes a write (in the draft, the resource's catalog row: open, or read-only with a reason), plus a memory bound on a server; reads do not pass the writer, so they go on. default.closes: a gate test in the phase that builds L2's refusals and the catalog row

default.why: E-02's pipeline, in TS, Rust and Go, writes every queued record with one writev and one fdatasync on a journal per process: 2.8 million 100 B appends a second on this disk, and 5.5 µs of CPU per append at 50,000 a second in TS. SLOG.closes: a pin on the log tier's journal, in the phase that builds it

The shared tier must also meet OPS-14, and its budget per tenant was not built (E-35). With a log tier per project that clause falls away.

BUY.why: Step 1: BUY's log is an outside program (nats-server). Step 2: `npm install fero` brings fero's client and libraries, not that program. Step 3: so `node app.ts` has no log to write to until someone installs and starts it. SPACE §4.2 states this by construction and E-44 confirms it in writing (its table, row 10); to ship and spawn the binary would make the row SRV with someone else's code.

default.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, DEP-21's $10 bar: the bar does not say where the 100 subscribers run. On Fly these rows cost $0.00 to $0.19 asleep (bar $2.19) and $4.94 to $7.26 at 10 writes/s with the subscribers inside, but $57.50 to $59.82 if each of 100 outside subscribers gets every write; the low end needs a shared tier or pool (J changed). Restated with the subscribers inside they sit 1.4 to 2 times under $10, on prices E-41 read from search summaries, which is not wide enough to call met.
default.closes: every price read again on the vendor's page (E-41's results/inputs.md), and the bar restated with the subscribers placed

OBJ.why: Q `put`: a commit is one PUT. At 10 writes/s, 100 ms apart, every write is its own commit: 26.3 million PUTs a month, $131 at $0.005 per 1,000, so $135.80 against $10 with the subscribers inside. That is 13.6 times the bar, too wide for a price read from a search summary to flip, and it is the same under AMENDMENTS 1.3's restated bar; fewer PUTs would mean a commit that waits over 2 s.

SRV.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3's DEP-21 line applies. Three servers and the app on two machines of its own cost $11.64 at 10 writes/s with the subscribers inside, 1.16 times the bar, on prices read from search summaries. With one app machine it would be $9.45, so this is not a failure by design.
SRV.closes: every price read again on the vendor's page (E-41's results/inputs.md), and the bar restated with the subscribers placed

PD.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3's DEP-21 line applies. Three servers, three controller machines and two app machines cost $18.21 at 10 writes/s with the subscribers inside, 1.8 times the bar. It leans to a failure, but the margin is under two times and rests on prices read from search summaries and on assumed machine counts.
PD.closes: every price read again on the vendor's page (E-41's results/inputs.md), and the bar restated with the subscribers placed
